transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-11
Time: 11:00 AM PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sara Kim (Head of ML, Riverbend), Daniel Ortega (CTO, Riverbend), Priya Shah (Security Lead, Riverbend), Liam Chen (Platform Eng)

Agenda: quick intros, onboarding timeline, security/compliance, infra integration (VPC/KMS), next steps

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Lee, AE at Redwood. With me today Priya our CSM and Mateo from solutions engineering.
00:10 Sara: Hi all, Sara here. Excited to get this kicked off.
00:14 Daniel: Daniel here, quick time check, we have about 42 minutes, right?
00:18 Jordan: Yep, 42. We'll cover high level then jump into security and infra.
00:30 Mateo: Quick note, Mateo from SE — I'll own the technical deep dive and any perf bench work, happy to pair with Liam.
00:40 Liam: Great.
00:45 Speaker 1: (mumbles) congrats on choosing Redwood, we saw good perf numbers.
01:05 Jordan: First, what's your primary success criteria for the first 30/60/90 days? Sara?
01:18 Sara: For us, 30 days is developers can call the hosted API in dev with anonymized data and validate core flows. 60 days is a POC on our staging with realistic traffic and some latency/cost numbers. 90 days is production pilot in a single region.
01:40 Priya Nair: That aligns with what we usually see. We'll build a success plan.
01:52 Daniel: A couple constraints: we need SOC2 alignment, data residency concerns for EU patients, and SSO through our Okta SAML. Also looking at dedicated vs hosted — cost is a concern, and some PHI flows may require private deployment.
02:18 Mateo: Understood. We support SAML/Okta for SSO and offer Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads. For PHI, customers often choose Redwood Private with KMS integration.
02:35 Priya Shah: On KMS — we need to know whether Redwood can integrate with our AWS KMS and whether HSM is supported for key material. Also audit logs and retention policies.
02:50 Mateo: We support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated customers; HSM integrations are typically via partner HSMs — I'll send a note with specifics. Audit logs: Console has token-level traces and we can export logs to your SIEM.
03:08 Jordan: We'll attach the compliance pack and SOC2 summary after the call.
03:20 Sara: Great. On the model side, we plan to start with the smaller open models for prototyping then evaluate higher accuracy models for pilot. We care about latency under 200ms for conversational flows, cost per 1k tokens in line with budgets.
03:40 Mateo: Sounds good. For latency, is 200ms p95 or median?
03:45 Sara: p95 ideally.
03:48 Mateo: Ok. For p95 under 200ms, we typically recommend Dedicated capacity or tuned hosted routes with caching and batching off for low-latency paths. We can run a perf benchmark with your token distribution.
04:12 Daniel: Speaking of benchmarks, how do you handle KV cache and prefix caching — we have token windows up to 4k?
04:25 Mateo: Our runtime supports KV cache for longer histories and continuous batching. For longer contexts we recommend quantized models on Dedicated GPUs to manage memory. I'll document best practices.
04:45 Sara: Is there a public pricing sheet for Dedicated? We need to compare with Anthropic and our internal self-hosted estimates.
04:52 Jordan: I'll send our Dedicated pricing summary and a cost model template. We'll include assumptions for batching, token lengths, and concurrency.
05:05 Priya Shah: One security question: can you do SSO just for the console but still use API keys for service accounts? We prefer SAML for user access.
05:20 Mateo: Yes, you can have SAML for console user auth and still issue service-level API keys for apps. Keys can be rotated and scoped by role.
05:32 Liam: On network side — we want VPC peering or private link. Do you support VPC peering into our AWS accounts?
05:40 Mateo: For Private deployments yes; for Dedicated we offer private connectivity options including VPC peering and PrivateLink depending on region. We'll capture your region and infra in the next step.
05:55 Sara: Our first pilot region is us-west-2 and EU-west-1 for EU residency.
06:02 Jordan: Noted. We'll ensure we capture data residency needs.
06:10 Speaker 2 (Robot): (background noise)
06:25 Priya Nair: Next, onboarding timeline. Our standard kickoffs have an initial week for account setup and test keys, week 2–3 for dev integration, week 4 for staging tests and bench, week 6–8 for pilot. Does that map to your expectations?
06:45 Daniel: That seems ok; we might accelerate if we can parallelize integration work.
07:00 Mateo: We can parallelize — while dev uses hosted test keys, infra can plan for VPC and KMS. We'll prepare a tech checklist.
07:15 Sara: On the data side, we will not send PHI to hosted endpoints during dev. We'll anonymize and only send synthetic/test data. Production pilot will require Private or Dedicated depending on compliance.
07:40 Priya Shah: Also want to confirm data retention settings, can logs be turned off or redacted?
07:50 Mateo: You can configure retention and redaction; in Private and Dedicated we can align retention to your policies. We'll include default retention notes in the compliance doc.
08:10 Jordan: I'll attach the compliance docs and the SOC2 summary, and also the onboarding checklist after this call.
08:22 Sara: Thanks. For the bench work — what's the expected lead time? If we want a perf report with our sample prompts, how long to run?
08:35 Mateo: Usually 1–2 weeks depending on complexity and load. If you provide a representative prompt set and token-length distribution, we can run a targeted benchmark. We'll need a point of contact for any test credentials.
08:50 Daniel: Liam will be the contact for infra and bench.
08:55 Liam: Yep.
09:05 Jordan: Great. Any questions about billing or contracts?
09:10 Daniel: Typical — we prefer monthly reserved capacity for Dedicated but want a trial run. How strict are commit terms?
09:20 Jordan: Commit terms are flexible; we offer trial credits on hosted and short-term evaluation windows for Dedicated before committing fully. We'll outline options in the deck.
09:32 Sara: Competitors — Anthropic came up, also considering OpenAI or internal self-hosted for cost reasons.
09:40 Jordan: Understood; we'll include a comparative note.
09:45 Mateo: Quick technical note: if you plan long contexts 4k+, quantization and model selection matter for latency; we'll propose a few model variants.
10:00 Priya Shah: For compliance we will require an exportable audit log for 90 days and SSO+RBAC. Also need details on data residency proof.
10:15 Mateo: We'll include an exportable audit log approach and RBAC mapping examples.
10:22 Sara: Excellent. Any blockers?
10:28 Daniel: Not yet. We need to review the contract language around data processing and subprocessor list.
10:35 Jordan: We'll send the DPA and subprocessor list with the compliance pack.
10:42 Speaker 3: (laughs)
10:50 Priya Nair: Recap of agreed next steps: Jordan will send onboarding deck + pricing, Mateo will prepare KMS/VPC notes and benchmark plan, Priya (CSM) will produce the 30-day success plan, Riverbend will share infra diagram and compliance items. We'll sync on scheduling the technical deep dive next week.
11:20 Sara: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
11:30 Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
11:40 End of call.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts (some speaker labels generic). Shared links to be sent: onboarding-deck.pdf (Jordan), dedicated-pricing.xlsx (Jordan), compliance-pack.pdf (Jordan), vpc-peering-guide.pdf (Mateo).
